Method of Attack: Displays fake ransomware messages with a timer labeled 'File Kill Timer' to scare users
Acts as a screenlocker rather than deleting files
Blocks execution of certain programs like Regedit, Task Manager, and CMD prompt by terminating their processes
Does not delete any files or configure autostart, infection ends on reboot
Impacted Systems: Windows systems (implied by mention of Regedit, Task Manager, CMD prompt)
Attack Vector: Execution of the malware program on the victim's computer
Indicators of Compromise: Screen displaying 'File Kill Timer' and messages from Smash! Ransomware
Blocked access to Regedit, Task Manager, CMD prompt
